encryption.title: Encryption at rest
encryption.description: Data on the internal disk and on backup destinations is unreadable without the owner's credentials.

firewall.title: Application firewall
firewall.description: Inbound connections are filtered and the machine does not answer probes it has no reason to answer.

integrity.title: Platform integrity
integrity.description: Gatekeeper, System Integrity Protection, the sealed system volume and XProtect are in their protective state.

updates.title: Software updates
updates.description: Security fixes and malware definitions arrive without waiting for a person to click.

login.title: Screen lock and login
login.description: An unattended or stolen session cannot be used without the password.

sharing.title: Sharing services
sharing.description: No remote access or file service listens unless it was turned on on purpose.

wireless.title: Bluetooth, AirDrop and Wi-Fi
wireless.description: Nearby radios do not expose the machine to strangers.

browser.title: Safari hygiene
browser.description: The default browser does not open downloads on its own and warns about known phishing sites.

identity.title: Credentials inventory
identity.description: Inventory facts about credential storage. Recorded for context, never scored.

ssh.title: SSH client
ssh.description: Keys and client configuration do not leak trust to other users or other hosts.

shell.title: Shell environment
shell.description: Shell history stays private and nothing on PATH can be replaced by another user.

packages.title: Third-party packages
packages.description: Package managers outside Apple's update channel are kept current.

checks.title: FileVault is enabled
checks.rationale: Without FileVault the internal disk can be read by anyone who holds the machine. A lost or stolen laptop becomes a data breach.
checks.expected: fdesetup reports FileVault is On and no decryption is in progress.
remediation: Open System Settings, Privacy and Security, FileVault, and choose Turn On.
Store the recovery key somewhere other than the laptop itself, or escrow it to your organisation.
Run `fdesetup status` again once encryption has finished.
references: CIS-style section: Privacy and Security, FileVault
Apple Platform Security guide: volume encryption with FileVault

checks.title: Time Machine destinations are encrypted
checks.rationale: A backup disk holds the same data as the laptop. An unencrypted backup undoes FileVault the moment the disk is lost.
checks.expected: Every configured Time Machine destination reports LastKnownEncryptionState = Encrypted, or no destination is configured.

evaluate.reason: No Time Machine destination is configured.
At least one destination is not encrypted.
No Time Machine destination is configured.

remediation: Open System Settings, General, Time Machine.
Remove the unencrypted destination and add it again with Encrypt Backup selected.
Keep the backup password in your password manager, not on the disk.

checks.title: Application firewall is enabled
checks.rationale: The application firewall blocks inbound connections to services nobody approved. It is the last filter on hostile networks such as hotels and conferences.
checks.expected: socketfilterfw reports State = 1 or State = 2.

evaluate.reason: Firewall is managed by a configuration profile and not readable here.

remediation: Open System Settings, Network, Firewall, and turn it on.
On a managed Mac, ask for the firewall payload in the configuration profile instead.

checks.title: Firewall stealth mode is enabled
checks.rationale: Stealth mode stops the Mac from answering ICMP and closed-port probes, which makes it harder to discover on a shared network.
checks.expected: socketfilterfw reports stealth mode on.

evaluate.reason: Firewall is managed by a configuration profile and not readable here.

remediation: Open System Settings, Network, Firewall, Options, and turn on Enable stealth mode.
The firewall itself must be on for stealth mode to have any effect.

checks.title: Firewall logging is enabled
checks.rationale: Firewall logs are the only local record of blocked inbound attempts. Without them an investigation starts blind.
checks.expected: socketfilterfw reports log mode on.

evaluate.reason: Firewall is managed by a configuration profile and not readable here.

remediation: Run `sudo /usr/libexec/ApplicationFirewall/socketfilterfw --setloggingmode on`.
On a managed Mac, enable logging in the firewall payload of the profile.

checks.title: Gatekeeper is enabled
checks.rationale: Gatekeeper refuses to launch downloaded software that is not signed and notarised. It is the first barrier against trojanised installers.
checks.expected: spctl reports assessments enabled.
remediation: Run `sudo spctl --global-enable`, or open System Settings, Privacy and Security, and allow apps from the App Store and identified developers.
If a single app needs an exception, approve that app instead of turning Gatekeeper off.
references: CIS-style section: Privacy and Security, Gatekeeper

checks.title: System Integrity Protection is enabled
checks.rationale: SIP stops even root from modifying protected system files and processes. With SIP off, malware that gains root can persist inside the operating system.
checks.expected: csrutil reports status enabled with no custom configuration.

evaluate.reason: SIP runs with a custom, partially disabled configuration.

remediation: Restart into macOS Recovery.
Open Terminal from the Utilities menu and run `csrutil enable`.
Restart and confirm with `csrutil status`.
references: Apple Platform Security guide: System Integrity Protection

checks.title: Sealed system volume is authenticated
checks.rationale: Authenticated root verifies the cryptographic seal of the system volume at boot. Disabling it allows a modified system to start without warning.
checks.expected: csrutil reports Authenticated Root status enabled.

evaluate.reason: The system volume seal is enforced.
The system volume seal is not enforced.

remediation: Restart into macOS Recovery.
Run `csrutil authenticated-root enable` in Terminal and restart.
references: Apple Platform Security guide: signed system volume

checks.title: XProtect definitions are present
checks.rationale: XProtect is the built-in signature scanner. If its bundle is missing, known malware families are not blocked at launch.
checks.expected: The XProtect bundle reports a numeric version.

evaluate.reason: The XProtect bundle was not found.

remediation: Turn on Install Security Responses and system files in System Settings, General, Software Update, Automatic Updates.
Run `softwareupdate --background` to fetch the latest definitions.
references: CIS-style section: Software updates, security responses

checks.title: Automatic update checks are enabled
checks.rationale: If macOS never checks for updates, nobody learns that a fix exists. Every other update control depends on this one.
checks.expected: AutomaticCheckEnabled is 1.

evaluate.reason: Not set locally. The macOS default or a configuration profile applies.

remediation: Open System Settings, General, Software Update, Automatic Updates, and turn on Check for updates.
Or run `sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.SoftwareUpdate AutomaticCheckEnabled -bool true`.

checks.title: Security responses and system files install automatically
checks.rationale: This setting delivers XProtect and other security data updates. Turning it off leaves malware definitions frozen at their last version.
checks.expected: ConfigDataInstall is 1.

evaluate.reason: Security data does not install automatically.
Not set locally. The macOS default or a configuration profile applies.

remediation: Open System Settings, General, Software Update, Automatic Updates, and turn on Install Security Responses and system files.
Or run `sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.SoftwareUpdate ConfigDataInstall -bool true`.
references: CIS-style section: Software updates, security responses

checks.title: Critical updates install automatically
checks.rationale: Rapid security fixes are only useful if they land without waiting for a person. Exploited vulnerabilities are often patched through this channel.
checks.expected: CriticalUpdateInstall is 1.

evaluate.reason: Critical updates wait for manual installation.
Not set locally. The macOS default or a configuration profile applies.

remediation: Open System Settings, General, Software Update, Automatic Updates, and turn on Install Security Responses and system files.
Or run `sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.SoftwareUpdate CriticalUpdateInstall -bool true`.

checks.title: macOS updates install automatically
checks.rationale: Point releases carry most security fixes. Machines that wait for a manual click fall weeks behind.
checks.expected: AutomaticallyInstallMacOSUpdates is 1.

evaluate.reason: macOS updates wait for manual installation.
Not set locally. The macOS default or a configuration profile applies.

remediation: Open System Settings, General, Software Update, Automatic Updates, and turn on Install macOS updates.
Or run `sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.SoftwareUpdate AutomaticallyInstallMacOSUpdates -bool true`.

checks.title: Screen lock requires a password
checks.rationale: When the screen saver starts or the lid closes, the session must not resume without the password. An unlocked laptop needs no exploit.
checks.expected: sysadminctl reports a screen lock delay rather than screen lock off.
remediation: Open System Settings, Lock Screen, and set Require password after screen saver begins or display is turned off.
Or run `sysadminctl -screenLock immediate -password -` and type your password when prompted.

checks.title: Screen lock engages within five seconds
checks.rationale: A long grace period lets someone wake an unattended laptop without a password. Five seconds covers an accidental screen saver and nothing more.
checks.expected: sysadminctl reports a delay of immediate or five seconds or less.

evaluate.reason: Screen lock delay is five seconds or less.
Screen lock delay is longer than five seconds.

remediation: Open System Settings, Lock Screen, and set Require password to Immediately.
Or run `sysadminctl -screenLock immediate -password -`.

checks.title: Screen saver starts within 20 minutes of inactivity
checks.rationale: The lock only helps if it starts. A screen saver set to never leaves the session open indefinitely.
checks.expected: idleTime is between 1 and 1200 seconds.

evaluate.reason: Not set for this user. The macOS default or a configuration profile applies.

evaluate.otherwise_reason: Screen saver starts after {value} seconds, or never when the value is 0.

remediation: Open System Settings, Lock Screen, and set Start Screen Saver when inactive to 20 minutes or less.
Or run `defaults -currentHost write com.apple.screensaver idleTime -int 600`.

checks.title: Automatic login is disabled
checks.rationale: Automatic login hands a full session to whoever opens the lid after a restart, and it is incompatible with FileVault protection at boot.
checks.expected: No autoLoginUser is configured for the login window.

evaluate.reason: No automatic login user is set.
An automatic login user is configured.

remediation: Open System Settings, Users and Groups, and set Automatically log in as to Off.
Or run `sudo defaults delete /Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow autoLoginUser`.
references: CIS-style section: Users and groups, login window

checks.title: Guest account is disabled
checks.rationale: The guest account gives anyone a local session without a password, which is a foothold for local privilege escalation.
checks.expected: GuestEnabled is 0 or not set.

evaluate.reason: Not set. The guest account is off by default.

remediation: Open System Settings, Users and Groups, Guest User, and turn off Allow guests to log in to this computer.
Or run `sudo defaults write /Library/Preferences/com.apple.loginwindow GuestEnabled -bool false`.
references: CIS-style section: Users and groups, guest account

checks.title: Remote Login (SSH server) is off
checks.rationale: An SSH server on a laptop is a network-reachable login prompt that roams across untrusted networks. Few laptops need one.
checks.expected: launchd reports com.openssh.sshd as disabled or not overridden.

evaluate.reason: Not overridden. Remote Login is off by default.

remediation: Open System Settings, General, Sharing, and turn off Remote Login.
If you need it, restrict it to named users and keep the firewall on.

checks.title: Screen Sharing is off
checks.rationale: Screen Sharing exposes a VNC-compatible service that grants full interactive control. It is a common target for password spraying.
checks.expected: launchd reports com.apple.screensharing as disabled or not overridden.

evaluate.reason: Not overridden. Screen Sharing is off by default.

remediation: Open System Settings, General, Sharing, and turn off Screen Sharing.
Use a brokered remote support tool that requires the user's consent per session instead.

checks.title: File Sharing (SMB server) is off
checks.rationale: An SMB server on a laptop publishes folders to every network it joins. Shared folders are rarely reviewed after the first use.
checks.expected: launchd reports com.apple.smbd as disabled or not overridden.

evaluate.reason: Not overridden. File Sharing is off by default.

remediation: Open System Settings, General, Sharing, and turn off File Sharing.
Share files through a managed cloud service with expiring links instead.

checks.title: Printer Sharing is off
checks.rationale: Printer Sharing runs a CUPS listener reachable from the local network. It adds attack surface for a feature laptops rarely need.
checks.expected: cupsctl reports _share_printers=0.
remediation: Open System Settings, General, Sharing, and turn off Printer Sharing.
Or run `cupsctl --no-share-printers`.

checks.title: Remote Apple Events are off
checks.rationale: Remote Apple Events let other machines drive applications on this one through AppleScript. The feature is rarely needed and easy to forget.
checks.expected: systemsetup reports Remote Apple Events: Off.
remediation: Open System Settings, General, Sharing, and turn off Remote Application Scripting.
Or run `sudo systemsetup -setremoteappleevents off`.
references: CIS-style section: Sharing, remote Apple events

checks.title: Bluetooth Sharing is off
checks.rationale: Bluetooth Sharing accepts files from nearby devices. It is a delivery channel for unsolicited content in public spaces.
checks.expected: PrefKeyServicesEnabled is 0 or not set.

evaluate.reason: Not set. Bluetooth Sharing is off by default.

remediation: Open System Settings, General, Sharing, and turn off Bluetooth Sharing.

checks.title: AirDrop is not discoverable by everyone
checks.rationale: AirDrop set to Everyone shows the device name to strangers and lets them push content. Contacts Only keeps the convenience without the exposure.
checks.expected: DiscoverableMode is Contacts Only or Off, or not set.

evaluate.reason: AirDrop is limited to contacts or off.
Not set. AirDrop defaults to Contacts Only.

remediation: Open Control Centre, AirDrop, and choose Contacts Only or Receiving Off.
Turn on Everyone for 10 Minutes only when you need it.

checks.title: Remembered Wi-Fi networks stay under 30
checks.rationale: Every remembered network is a name the laptop will join automatically. A long list of hotel and café networks makes evil twin attacks easy.
checks.expected: The Wi-Fi interface remembers 30 networks or fewer.
remediation: Open System Settings, Wi-Fi, Advanced, and remove networks you no longer use.
Turn off Auto-Join for public networks you keep.

checks.title: Safari does not open downloaded files automatically
checks.rationale: Open safe files after downloading runs archives and documents without a decision from the user. Several drive-by chains have relied on it.
checks.expected: AutoOpenSafeDownloads is 0.

evaluate.reason: Not readable. Safari settings live in a sandbox container that needs Full Disk Access, or the default applies.

remediation: Open Safari, Settings, General, and clear Open safe files after downloading.

checks.title: Safari warns about fraudulent websites
checks.rationale: The fraudulent website warning blocks known phishing pages before credentials are typed.
checks.expected: WarnAboutFraudulentWebsites is 1.

evaluate.reason: Not readable. Safari settings live in a sandbox container that needs Full Disk Access, or the default applies.

remediation: Open Safari, Settings, Security, and select Warn when visiting a fraudulent website.

checks.title: iCloud Keychain sync is present (inventory)
checks.rationale: Knowing whether a synced password store exists helps decide where to recommend credentials live. The probe records presence only and never reads items or account names.
checks.expected: The signed-in account lists the keychain sync service as enabled.

evaluate.reason: An iCloud account is signed in without keychain sync.
No iCloud account is signed in.

remediation: No action is required. This is an inventory item.
If your organisation standardises on a different password manager, record that instead.
references: CIS-style section: Apple account and iCloud

checks.title: SSH directory and private keys are private
checks.rationale: If ~/.ssh or a private key is readable by other local users, any compromised account on the machine inherits your access to every server.
checks.expected: ~/.ssh is 0700, private keys and authorized_keys are not group or world accessible.
remediation: Run `chmod 700 ~/.ssh`.
Run `chmod 600` on every private key and on `~/.ssh/authorized_keys`.

checks.title: SSH client configuration keeps host verification
checks.rationale: StrictHostKeyChecking no, a known hosts file of /dev/null, or agent forwarding to every host turns a single malicious server into access to all the others.
checks.expected: ~/.ssh/config does not disable host key checking and does not forward the agent to Host *.
remediation: Remove `StrictHostKeyChecking no` and `UserKnownHostsFile /dev/null` from `~/.ssh/config`.
Move `ForwardAgent yes` under the specific Host entries that need it, or use ProxyJump instead.

checks.title: SSH private keys are protected by a passphrase
checks.rationale: An unencrypted private key on disk is a credential that any process running as you can copy. A passphrase, or a hardware-backed key, keeps a stolen file useless.
checks.expected: Every private key in ~/.ssh is encrypted.
remediation: Add a passphrase with `ssh-keygen -p -f <key file>` and store it in the macOS keychain with `ssh-add --apple-use-keychain`.
Better still, move to a hardware-backed key such as a FIDO2 security key (`ssh-keygen -t ed25519-sk`).

checks.title: Shell history files are private
checks.rationale: Shell history routinely captures tokens and passwords typed on the command line. Other local users must not be able to read it.
checks.expected: History files in the home directory are not group or world readable.
remediation: Run `chmod 600` on each history file listed in the finding.
Prefer environment files or a secret manager over typing secrets into the shell.
references: CIS-style section: User environment, home directory

checks.title: No writable or relative directories in PATH
checks.rationale: If any directory on PATH is world-writable, or PATH contains a relative entry, another user or a downloaded archive can plant a binary that runs instead of the real one.
checks.expected: Every PATH entry is absolute and none is world-writable.
remediation: Remove `.` and empty entries from PATH in your shell profile.
Run `chmod o-w` on each world-writable directory listed in the finding, or drop it from PATH.

checks.title: Homebrew packages are mostly current
checks.rationale: Homebrew sits outside Apple's update channel. Outdated formulae and casks accumulate known vulnerabilities silently.
checks.expected: brew outdated lists 10 packages or fewer.

evaluate.reason: {value} outdated packages, within the limit of 10.
evaluate.otherwise_reason: {value} outdated packages, above the limit of 10.

remediation: Run `brew update && brew upgrade`.
Remove packages you no longer use with `brew autoremove` and `brew uninstall`.
references: CIS-style section: Software updates, third-party software
